items.quote:
“A beautiful shell with not much soul beneath.”
Ghost of Yotei starts strong visually — the graphics are beautiful, the lighting and environments are genuinely impressive, and for a while, that alone carries the experience. But beneath the surface, it’s mostly hollow. The world feels reasonably empty, padded with repetitive chores and side activities that add length but little **** story is yet another revenge tale — one we’ve seen reheated dozens of times before. It tries to explore deeper emotions, but it never quite commits. The so-called “bonding” scenes with Kiku feel forced, as if the writers wanted to inject some humanity into Atsu’s otherwise one-dimensional revenge arc. Sure, seeing Atsu soften a bit and find some purpose through her niece adds a touch of warmth, but it also completely dilutes the core motive of vengeance. By the end, she feels more like a conflicted terminator who forgot what she was fighting for in the first place.Characters overall lack depth. In Ghost of Tsushima, you could form real emotional connections — here, most of them feel like side quests with dialogue. The only truly memorable character was Oyuki, who at least had some weight to her **** final act drags on far too long. The spider/dragon sequence and the extended chase with Lord Saito feel like artificial padding — spectacle for spectacle’s **** the end of the day, Ghost of Yotei is technically polished but narratively hollow. It looks great, plays fine, but struggles to make you care.
Verdict: Gorgeous visuals can’t hide a recycled story and shallow emotional beats. Enjoyable in short bursts, forgettable in the long run.

items.quote: After obtaining the platinum trophy and having almost 100% completion, Ghost of Yotei is a good standalone sequel to GoT, but I would say that that game is slightly better in my opinion (I gave that game a 9 in my original review). While I did enjoy Yotei, the story and characters are weaker this time around. It’s your typical revenge story where the protagonist wants to kill someone who wronged them in some way and about 70% into the story the whole “revenge is bad” trope comes up. Nothing that I haven’t seen before in my 15+ years of playing video games. Atsu is just OK, I don’t dislike her, but I certainly did not like her as much as I liked Jin. As far as the open world exploration goes, this is one of the things that GoY does much better than Tsushima in my opinion. There’s a lot more variety to side missions and side quests instead of just analyzing some areas like a crime scene investigator and then following footprints. The game rewards exploration in the form of charms, armor, points to acquire new skills, etc. There’s now a crafting system to allow players to craft consumable items such as smoke bombs, arrows, ammo for your guns, etc. I also liked the addition of new melee weapons instead of just being limited to a **** my biggest point of criticism with the game is how unbalanced the damage values are in Medium difficulty and how unbalanced the duels are in general. Duel opponents and strong enemies can easily kill you in 2-3 hits, but Atsu must hit them a dozen times before they drop. I cannot stand games that do this. This would not be a complaint if I was playing on Hard, but I wasn’t, I was playing on Medium. Takezo the Unrivaled is by far the worst offender of this and it is by far one of the most **** boss fights that I have ever seen in a  video game, period. I ended up switching the difficulty to Custom 30 hours into my playthrough and had to switch to Casual to beat Takezo. I don’t know what the heck **** Punch was thinking when adjusting the enemy damage values, but it seems to me like they copied and pasted the enemy damage values of the Iki Island expansion from GoT to this game. Its still a good game, but Tsushima is slightly better for the above mentioned reasons.

Watching her evolve — not just as a warrior but as a person — was incredibly empowering. Her growth, strength, and resilience felt real and raw, and I connected with her journey on so many levels. The story pulled me in emotionally from start to finish, and by the time the credits rolled, I was heartbroken. I cried. PS5 Pro

items.quote:
Being a pretty hardcore fan of Ghost of Tsushima, and having hoped for a sequel since a week after GoT's release, this was a bit of a disappointment
It is a good game indeed, but it is nowhere near as good as it's predecessor.
What made Tsushima so great was the story, which was refreshingly original and heavy, with good pacing, character development and twist and turns. 
Yotei lacks this in the worst way, unfortunatelly. 
Atsu's story is a plethora of tired ideas, each one worse than the one before, making it an all too often cringy kind of Dungeons&Dragons-esque mess of clichés and overused plot directions. 
Her character and motivation beyond revenge is hard to pin down, making it hard to get to know her. She is morally ambiguous, which is not necessarily a bad thing as far as open-world game characters go, but in this case I found her really unlikeable, and that in turn made her and her mission hard to care for

I did, however, enjoy the fleshed out open-world, offering a wide range of activities and sidequests, even if the art direction of the world is less capticating and awe-inspiring than the first game's. 

The combat system is okay, even though I preferred the old game's stance-system over the new weapon-swaps system. 
This new system, along with many new moves, makes the combat more advanced, but it comes with a toll, which is that the combat feels way less fluent than in Tsushima. 
This is a shame because when I played GoT, I could be fully engaged in combat and still enjoy the spectacle on the screen. 
In GoY, there is so much more going on that fully enjoying the beautiful choreography and motions of the characters is all but impossible.

Lots more to say, for better or worse, but that's the jist.

I don´t know why everyone is putting 9s and 10s to this game. Don´t get me wrong, it is a good game, but is barely better than Tsushima in some ways but lacking in some areas too. The 86 is a perfectly good note for this game, truly. 

The good:
It plays marvelous and the combat is as good if not better as Tsushima.
The visual style is GORGEOUS, like not a single game in PS Studios on Ps5 use the colors like Yotei, truly beautifull.
The weapon trowing mechanic is so fun and a good addition to the game.
The majority of emotional moments are far better than Tsushima, you actually feel for the characters.
The music is oustanding and a step up from Tsushima.
The open world is really organic and fun to actually explore.
The drip in the armors were upgraded.

The bad:

The writting goes to the abbys after chapter 2 and it was showing its cracks at the Kitsune´s storyline. Chapter 2 and 3 are so bad compared to the first chapter that it genuinely gives you the feeling that they wanted to do more but didn´t have the time.

You can erase almost 3/4 of the entire cast of characters that appears in the "wolf pack" and the game is the same... 

The "wolf" theme of the game is dissapointing AT BEST. The story doesn´t explain the wolf, doesn´t even use the wolf in the story too.

The revenge cliché is EXACTLY as you think it would go in the story, nothing remotely new or creative, you already watched this plot.
For some reason Atsu is mischaracterized after chapter 2.

The shrines and fox dents are SO BORING just like Tsushima.

The stealth, just like Tsushima, is bad, somehow in this game is worse thanks to the level design.

The ending doesn´t have even an ounce of the impact that Ghost of Tsushima has. It has no buildup, the final battle is thematically horrendous, it does not make sense in any way.

Atsu  forgets and remembers that she has fire arms in the story, it was a mistake to put them in the game if you´re not gonna to use them.

In conclusion:

The game is good, but i expected a lot more to be honest. You feel like half of the themes in the game are undercooked and it is a shame.
It´s almost the same game as Tsushima, with the good, and suprisingly, with new bads.
If you liked Tsushima and wanted more, play this game, but don´t expect a better story in any possible way.

items.quote: This game is not bad. But it's worse than Ghost of Tsushima in almost every way. I'm a big fan of GoT: played it three times, including 2 on lethal difficulty, got the platinum trophy. Yotei's story and characters pale in comparison. Everything seems shallow and rushed. They tried to create a "Japanese western" revenge plot, but they don't build up the emotions needed for you to care for this revenge. It's hard to care for a revenge story that you're not deeply immersed in. The characters make everything worse. There are very few good characters, and the protagonist is not one of them. Jin Sakai was a superior protagonist, more human, relatable and fleshed out. The villains' motives are never really explained. They're just a bunch of bad dudes doing bad things. As for the gameplay, the game is way harder than GoT, in every bad way. On harder difficulties the battles are unfair and not fun. On the normal difficulty they're too easy, and enemies are kind of dumb. Combat mechanics are more varied than GoT, but here we have a perfect example of "more is less". They've just added too much: weapons, moves, tricks, tools etc. I would be happier with another GoT DLC. I'm kinda sad, now that I've finished the game, because I really tried to enjoy it. I sank over 40 hours in it. Finished all the side quests, got all the abilities. Everything is repetitive and the fun runs out pretty quick. Graphics are good, but Tsushima is better. I always prefer art direction over graphical fidelity, and GoT had better art direction. Music is really good, can't complain here. But overall, this is a very mixed and average game. If you've played GoT, adjust your expectations.

The story being wafer thin just makes her kind of pointless. **** could have elected to make a create a character for this game and it would have made no difference to this. 

And this is a standalone sequel, that heavily relies on the vibes of the prior game to make you want to care about this one; and I just don't. It's too open ended, too bland, and ultimately not going to be memorable enough for me past a few weeks after beating it. Ghost of Tsushima is the vastly superior title, it's not even close.

items.quote:
A Worthy Successor That Stops Just Short of GreatnessThe Return of the Samurai SpiritGhost of Yotei is, in every sense, the spiritual successor to Ghost of Tsushima. From its engine to its windswept environments and familiar combat cadence, it feels like coming home — but maybe to a home that hasn’t been redecorated in a while. **** Punch Studios once again immerses players in feudal Japan, though this time through the eyes of Atsu, a woman driven by vengeance after the slaughter of her **** story beats are classic — perhaps too classic. It’s a revenge tale painted with the same moral brush as its predecessors: “Let go of the past, choose peace, find the future.” While the performances and writing are solid, the narrative doesn’t quite reach the emotional heights or historical intrigue of Tsushima. That game unearthed an overlooked chapter of Japan’s history; Yotei merely retells a familiar one. It’s effective, but predictable.A major issue lies in the antagonist’s world — it feels unnaturally centered around Atsu, as though every villainous act was staged for her benefit. Compared to Sifu, which made its nameless revenge story hit harder through ambiguity and realism, Yotei’s world feels a bit too self-aware. The story is good — just not great.Gameplay: Sharpened, But Not ReinventedMechanically, Ghost of Yotei plays it safe. Swordplay and stealth are still the cornerstones, with combat feeling fluid, responsive, and rewarding. Parrying remains satisfying, and the blend of Assassin’s Creed-style exploration and Dark Souls-inspired dueling gives each encounter weight. But after five years of anticipation, the lack of innovation stings.There’s nothing wrong with the combat — it’s above average, even thrilling at times — but the absence of a bold, new mechanic makes it feel iterative rather than evolutionary. Yotei is the kind of game you enjoy deeply in the moment, but rarely marvel at.Graphics and PerformanceVisually, Ghost of Yotei is beautiful — but in a nostalgic way. The PS5’s power is evident in ray-traced lighting and lush particle effects, yet something about the world feels dated. While reflections shimmer realistically and weather transitions are smooth, the overall fidelity doesn’t reach the jaw-dropping realism of Red Dead Redemption 2 or God of War ****’ll still stop to take photos, but you might not feel compelled to frame them.Music and AtmosphereThe score deserves praise for cultural authenticity, layering traditional Japanese instruments and folk rhythms to strong emotional effect. However, much of it fades into the background. The game’s attempts at teaching cultural and historical tidbits are admirable but occasionally intrusive, halting pacing for lessons that don’t always enrich the narrative. It’s informative, yes, but not always impactful.VerdictGhost of Yotei is a polished, passionate follow-up that does almost everything right — except surprise you. It’s a technically proficient, emotionally resonant, and culturally respectful samurai epic that nonetheless plays things too **** Punch delivers yet another strong title worthy of your time, but after Tsushima’s groundbreaking debut, Yotei feels content to echo greatness rather than redefine it.

Beautiful, heartfelt, and expertly crafted — but lacking the innovation to make it legendary.

items.quote: Ghost of Yotei is everything I wanted from a samurai game. items.author: crashpal

items.quote:
The Ghost of Yotei's formula, while similar to its predecessor in several ways (all good), sets itself apart by taking things to new heights, which helps provide a very fresh and immersive experience. The game throws you into the role of Atsu and offers immediate insight into her tale of vengeance across the wilderness of Ezo. The setting of the game alone makes it worth the purchase, with the combination of strong visuals and a relaxing soundtrack while riding your horse or playing your shamisen.
Combat feels deeper and more engaging as you switch from various weapons like the slower heavy-hitting odachi to the faster dual-katanas or the kursarigama. The open world once again offers plenty to explore with numerous side activities to dive into for seemingly endless gameplay outside of the main story. It's not perfect, as some side-quests fall into familiar tropes, and the pacing can be a bit slow at times.
Overall, Ghost of Yotei is a compelling, high-quality action-adventure game that pushes the PS5 hardware and rewards the player for their exploration and combat equally. If you own a PS5 and played Ghost of Tsushima, or like samurai-themed games, then this one is a must-have.

items.quote:
A game so good I felt the need to create a metacritic account to talk about it

The game is just a beautiful experience from start to finish and improves in almost every category vs it's predecessor Tsushima. SPunch has refined the gameplay from the first game and brought it to new heights. In the future I would love to see how they further expand for the combat. As for the story, I was enthralled and blown away by the immersive performances, realistic character dynamics and the music, oh my goodness the music is INCREDIBLE. If someone prefers the story of Jin in the first game as opposed to this one that is totally okay. I myself however prefer the story in Yotei. A classic story of revenge, mercy and what it means to grieve. I initially wanted to give it an 8, however no game has left me wanting to sit down and finish it all the way through before moving on quite like this game. And that alone deserves extra points from me (someone who has trouble finishing games with an extensive backlog). After completing the main story last night I still can't wait to go home and complete the quest I left unfinished. The world has this beautiful way of pulling you in, getting invested with the characters and I have never EVER felt the need to use photo mode in a video game but this game I found myself playing with the photo mode on various occasions. I highly recommend this game and it was worth every penny. My only hope is that SPunch adds a new game plus so I can experience the game and the story again in Japanese Black and White for a completely different experience without the need to level up my character. If you read this far, I appreciate you and I hope you love this game as much as I have.

items.quote: Ghost of Yotei isn’t just a project — it’s an experience. Every frame feels intentional, every sound carries emotion, and every transition hits like a heartbeat. It’s not just about visuals; it’s about atmosphere. You can feel the cold wind of Yotei, the silence before movement, the calm before the storm. The camera doesn’t just capture — it breathes with the subject. There’s a balance between chaos and serenity, precision and freedom. The color grading, the pacing, the storytelling — it all screams mastery. Ghost of Yotei feels like a love letter to perfection, a statement that style can carry meaning, that minimalism can be powerful. It’s cinematic poetry, crafted with care and vision. Watching it isn’t passive; it pulls you in, makes you feel part of the world it builds. Ghost of Yotei doesn’t just impress — it haunts you, long after the final shot fades.

items.quote:
A stunning story and visuals, an updated UI, and the long-awaited continuation of the Ghost of Tsushima saga - and sadly, that’s where the highlights end.

The combat system feels like it was designed by a team that has never actually played their own game. Parry and dodge timings are completely broken, block breaking is slower, and overall fight fluidity took a huge hit. The overloaded weapon mechanics the game forces on you only make things worse. I wish it gave me more freedom - like ignoring the yari entirely and just investing deeper into katana skills. After all, this is supposed to be a new game, not a DLC (though it sure feels like one).

Most assets, animations, and mechanics are straight copy-pasted from the previous entry with only a thin layer of minor tweaks. Exploration is once again painfully slow. The world is massive, but your movement speed without a horse kills any desire to travel on foot.

Lighting is both breathtaking and occasionally ridiculous. Outdoors, it’s beautiful. Indoors, the blinding light sources feel like the second coming of the sun.Fire starting, cooking, and weapon upgrading mini-games are fun for the first hour - then it just feels like the devs get a tip every time I waste more time on them. Climbing mechanics remain as bad as ever.

Taken together, it feels like a large “alternative DLC” dressed up as a AAA sequel. Nothing fundamental was fixed, and some of the best parts of the original were made worse.

And yet… it’s still worth playing and grinding to platinum. Just don’t expect the same magic as the first game.

PS: Game finished and I can say it even worse than i think, main story take about 8 hours in general, and other 40 world exploring. Stupid delays in animation, totally broken key bindings which make me press R2 so many times when i want jump on the horse, but it climb, open weapon menu, but not action what i want. This is total rubbish for scam game funs. Only designers did their job well, all other departments should be fired. Im done, no more pre-orders

items.quote: Ghost of Yōtei is a well-crafted game, almost bug-free at launch. The DualSense on PS5 is perfectly adapted — every vibration, sword movement, and step feels realistic and alive. The graphics are high-quality, with many places that are simply beautiful to look at. The sound is excellent. The combination of visuals and audio lets you slip into a meditative state — it feels calm and deeply **** combat system seems easy at first, but once you face the bosses you realize that real skill is required. This adds interest and motivation to learn and refine your fighting techniques, develop your abilities, and explore the map further. The combat has a true Japanese character — precise, disciplined, and **** story has a psychological tone. It’s not layered and confusing like Elden Ring, where you spend hours figuring out who betrayed whom. Here it’s different — a story about motivation, inner scars, and the attempt to heal psychological wounds while walking the path of vengeance. The deeper you go, the more you face your own fears and your past self.Through my own initiative, I use AI alongside the game — I take photos of buildings, objects, and details with my phone and show them to AI. It explains what they are, why they were built, and what they mean in Japanese culture. This makes the experience even deeper — I start to understand the history, traditions, and spirit of Japan in that era, feeling the culture not just through gameplay but through real knowledge.

items.quote:
Ghost of Yotei features many of the strengths which made Ghost of Tsushima a generational classic, but suffers from a markedly inferior main story, weaker character writing, and an inferior level of polish on its gameplay innovations compared to its predecessor.

Story and character writing: 5/10

The main story and character arc of the protagonist, Atsu, promises a story of trauma, vengeance, and redemption; however, severe pacing issues, odd structural choices in the ordering of story elements, and a weaker supporting cast than Ghost of Tsushima fail to deliver on its promise. Likewise, the cast of villains are handled clumsily. Their appearances are extremely brief, collectively featuring for less screentime than Khotun Khan alone sees during Ghost of Tsushima. This is an especially odd choice since Atsu's conflict with these characters is entirely personal, yet their interactions are short and stifled. Side quest content is more varied and of higher quality than in Tsushima, but this does not redeem the failings of the plot.

Gameplay: 8.5/10

Ghost of Yotei's gameplay is highly similar in fundamentals to Ghost of Tsushima. The stance system of the first game, enabling the player to target specific enemy weaknesses, is replaced by an arsenal of different weapons filling the same general roles. The greater intrinsic variety provided by these different weapons is welcome and all of the weapons play well and are usable, but are not evenly balanced. Gear design choices limit build diversity compared to Tsushima; the gameplay-altering effects available through armor sets and charms - the game's other kind of build crafting equipment slot - are less pronounced than in Tsushima. Where almost every armor set (each featuring three effects as a collection, each of which is generally more gameplay-altering when compared to the individually selectable single-effect charms) in Tsushima opened up an entirely new playstyle, the effects of each armor are much more subtle in Yotei.

Several changes to basic combat and enemy design show a lower level of polish than Tsushima. The game plays fairly well on medium difficulty, but it seems as if the game was not playtested at all on other difficulty settings. Enemies are generally spongy while the Atsu is much frailer than Jin; this effect is by far at its worst in boss fights, where bosses often require 30 or more hits to defeat against the player's 1-2. Enemy aggression is also much higher, while player defensive tools are weaker. Enemies react inconsistently to player actions, in many cases unpredictably ignoring well-timed counters. Enemy attacks have absurd tracking, frequently resulting in enemies sliding across large distances and comically spinning mid-attack animation in order to hit the player. Perhaps most disappointingly, some of the player's own new combat tools such as the katana's timed heavy attack string are lethargic and extremely difficult to actually use. In total, the game encourages a much more passive, slower paced, and less exciting approach to combat compared to Tsushima.

The gameplay is still quite good and is the game's largest strength, but would benefit from a great deal of tweaking in patches.

Visuals, the world, and aesthetics: 9.5/10.

Ghost of Yotei is beautiful. The striking colors, patterns, and variety of player cosmetics and the world itself deliver again at the highest level. The composition of these elements in the world is expert. 

The lone weakness in the visual and world design of the game is the presence of artificial barriers lining and defining each region of the game. If exploring the edges of any section of the map, you will often find yourself pressed up against the same bush repeated for hundreds of feet, forming a perfectly impassable wall. While not typically an issue, it is a very noticeably game-y element in an otherwise good world.

Дальше описание основной моей боли и мпойлеры. Сюжет - это просто кошмар. Насколько мне понравилась первая часть, настолько не понравилось продолжение. Все предсказуемо и безвкусно. Как только один из персонажей заикнулся, что у него есть дорогой ему человек, я его похоронил. И я удивился, когда он дожил до конца игры и даже не стал участвовать в финальной битве. НО НЕТ. В первой части было много трагедии, но произведение абсолютно обоснованно и ко всем последствиям приводилирешения персонажей и череда их решений. Лицемерие современной индустрии. DLC, лично мне, не нужно.

items.quote: This game shined with its gameplay, boss fights, and story, with graphics being a strong runner up.  Ghosts of Tsushima was gorgeous but I found the gameplay and story lacking.  Ghosts of Yotei, while still beautiful, I found it had a more dreary, less colorful bleak feeling, which may have been their goal.  However, the gameplay, especially the boss fights, we're extremely challenging but not crazy impossible.  No 2 story quests, either main quest or side quest, felt the same (like most Ubisoft games quests), and whats most important to me, the story, had me completely wrapped up in it.  The story took me completely by surprise.  Based on how I felt about Ghost of Tsushima story, I came into this expecting to have a mediocre story.  Even with the dark beginning, it didnt really grab me. But it didnt take long before Atsu had me.  I sometimes felt for the antagonist.  Reading Saitos letters along the way made me feel like he wasnt completely unjustified.  I thought the Spider would be a drunken spoiled annoying brat, but when his time came, I even felt for him. When a story makes me feel for the protagonist as well as the antagonist, I feel like they did a good job.  Atsu, Jubei, Oriyoku, Kiku, Saito, the Spider, Takezo the Undefeated, and especially Mad Goro, all well written characters.  Some of these characters were brief side quests but had well enough written parts that I really enjoyed interacting with them.  Great job on this game.  It didnt do anything really incredible or new, the painting was dumb, music was meh but served an in-game purpose, but kind of felt like just random filler content.  I really was not expecting to like this game as much as i did. I never finished Ghosts of Tsushimas 2nd island, but i couldn't put Ghosts of Yotei down til it was finished.  Id give it a good 9 out of 10.  Well done!

items.quote:
Ghost of Yotei is a brilliant game with addictive gameplay. I didn't play Ghost of Tsushima before soI didn't know what I was getting into but the game immediatly captured me in it's magnificient world. The game starts with a cutscene immediatly introducing the main character Atsu and her motivations in an abstract way. The night of the burning tree - the initial cutscene doesn't give us much information about what happened that night but you get more information how every member of the Yotei Six- the antagonists of the game - were involved as the story progresses . After the inital cutscene Atsu writes down every name of said Yotei Six and starts her hunt on the first one. The first fight was weirdly memorable as it sets the stage to the amazing combat system this game has.
After that fight she returns homefor the first time in years, the game utilizes a neat mechanic of switching between the present and past to show more tutorials and give the player better insight of her life before that night. After that you're free to roam the world.
The world isn't the biggest but it still feels so crowded in it's emptiness. Bamboo Stands, hot springs etc are scattered everywhere and are extremely fun to do and find. While riding around looking all around the map for these places you will every here and there stop to just admire thelooks of everything. the art direction for this game was more than just breathtaking. It took me 25h before I even went for the second boss as the world just had so much to offer.
The Gameplay is easily a 10 out of 10 for me. Through Atsus journey you obtain a variety of weapons each having their own strenghts and weaknesses. With the combination of the long range and quickfire weapons you always have the choice to make your gameplay thrilling and different with every enemy you encounter- play stealthy or storm in head on. It never bored me a second while playing.
The story of the game follows a simple revenge story with a few twists here and there. But nothing too special. And that's what bothers me. All the characters felt flat at points. Sometimes it went into themes of identity but then switched it up. Many of the characters especially the Yotei Six are just plot devices. We barely get to know these epic villains. Let's take the Dragon for example - he is known to be the prefered brother of the two but almost has no screen time. The dynamic between the Saito brothers isn't completely established and their love for each other is not notable at all until the Dragon falls so early. He is only a plot device to later on establish the Spider more as a character. And that is unfortunatly not the only case.
I just really wish we will soon get a NG+ update which lets you have every weapon from the beginning, more camps, keeping the cosmetics, harder gameplay as well as give us more insight into the characters especially the Yotei Six. As a NG+ is set up for a second playthrough where the player is already familiar with the game and story, additional cutscenes would make that second run really enjoyable. I hope the Update comes soon. But overall a recommendation for anyone looking for a capturing and thrilling open-world experience.

items.quote:
Open-world games in the "Ubisoft stlye" are seldom true greats, so full to the brim with stuff for the player to do that the resulting experience can lack the overall coherence needed to create something timeless. Storytelling often suffers the most, with the goal of "player freedom" and the sheer variety of gameplay elements on offer regularly clashing with the needs of a well-crafted narrative. Occasionally, though, one of these games manages to thread the needle, marrying the gameplay contrivances of the open-world genre with narratives and characters that suit the structure, rather than struggle against it

Ghost of Yōtei is far closer to one of the latter, standing above many of its open world peers, with even many minor side missions featuring thematic resonance with its main story or protagonist Atsu's personal journey from vengeful force of nature fueled by ruminating in her grief to a woman with something more to live for than revenge

While Ghost of Yōtei's story of revenge, grief, and trauma is not necessarily revolutionary in the modern landscape of video games, it is written and conveyed with a level of care far beyond that of similar open world games (with comparisons to other recent open world titles set in Japan with many similar narrative elements being hard to avoid). The game's side quests serve primarily to frame and flesh out its central narrative, enriching the entire experience for thoroughly-minded players

Like other open world games of this sort, Ghost of Yōtei does feature optional "checklist" content, but each of these is attached strongly to Atsu's character and emotional core (from painting sumi-e or playing shamisen as a way to remember her family to climbing mountain shrines like that of Mount Yōtei, which would have been something of a coming of age ritual for her in another life). This framing serves to ground these activities and make them feel far less extraneous than is typical, while not going so far as to make them essential for the uninterested

In addition to its solid storytelling, Ghost of Yōtei features great combat, which gets to shine all the more thanks to its casting off of RPG progression systems that have come to plague the genre in recent memory. Instead, the player is giving an array of tools, trinkets, and armor sets suited for different playstyles (with the normal open world trinity of melee, ranged, and stealth taking center stage) and encouraged to play around with what's available to them to succeed, in addition to mastering combat basics like perfect parries, dodge rolls, and the like. On their own, many of these tools, from bows and throwing knives and firearms and different melee weapons are par for the course for the genre, but divorced from RPG-like gearing and progression systems, they feel fresh and can shine on their own merits

But perhaps where Ghost of Yōtei shines the most is in its audio-visual presentation, which features a vibrant world awash with color and beauty, accented with a musical score that is often content to let the player take in their surroundings accompanied only by ambience. These elements are additionally used as gameplay, guiding players to objectives without the distraction of copious quest markers and waypoints, creating an immersive experience nigh unrivaled in this genre space (except perhaps by its predecessor, Ghost of Tsushima)

The cherry on top is perhaps that Ghost of Yōtei is the first game of this generation that feels properly "next-gen. Impressive motion capture and stunning graphical quality (bolstered by incredible art direction) make the game actually look like it's truly using the capabilities of the latest PlayStation in a way that even other Sony exclusives have struggled to do for most of this console generation

Ultimately, in a modern landscape where the open world genre seems to be losing some of its luster, Ghost of Yōtei serves as a reminder that such games can and should be great experiences, and indeed, more than the sum of their parts

items.quote: Though the game is quite similar to the first installment in the franchise, it was still a truly amazing experience. The story, which many where iffy about before launch, was absolutely amazing, though it was more generally "generic" in terms of style, being a revenge plot instead of Tsushima's struggle with the samurai code, it still was a masterpiece. [SPOILER] The decision to kill off Jubei at the end is my only gripe with the plot, as I feel it would have made more sense for Oyuki to jump in in an act of possible redemption for her past actions especially towards Atsu and Jubei, as well as Jubei's plans to be a father could have likely made him feel the urge to stay with and protect Kiku. The open world is ten times better than in Tsushima though, the world feeling alive, I especially love the way you obtain quests and information about the Yotei Six, through interrogation of enemies and people who show up to your camp. One thing that is sort-of a double-edged sword is the new "stance" system. I love the inclusion of multiple melee weapons such as the katana, dual katana, yari, odachi, and kusarigama, I feel like it could have been implemented in a different way than in a manner to replace stances, though I can see how it makes sense, so it really is no big deal. There are many activities to do that don't feel repetitive and/or are fun to complete, other than maybe the huge abundance of altars of reflections. Can't wait for Legends in 2026 and hopefully a DLC sometime in the near future!

items.quote:
A competent but empty open-world game. The first entry was overrated, a solid 7/10 at best, and this sequel just copies the same template. Climbing is repetitive and nowhere near what the new Zeldas established as good climbing mechanics, zero sense of risk or reward. The world looks fine but feels lifeless, the combat is good, and every system plays like deja vu from the last twenty years of open-world design.

Open-world games have become stagnant, bloated with checklist mechanics and meaningless exploration. Developers keep mistaking scale for depth. “Closed-world” games like Bloodborne or the Souls series are better at this point, they have tighter spaces, deliberate pacing, and strong atmosphere that can deliver more immersion than any procedural map full of icons. Ghost of Yotei follows the wrong lesson, it expands the map, not the soul.
Technically polished yet emotionally hollow. Play it only if you have nothing else to do.

items.quote: I finished my first playthrough and 100% the game after 60 hours. I first played the previous game, Ghost of Tsushima, back in 2021. That was one of the best video games I have ever played, and it was genuinely a masterpiece. Ever since I played that game, I've been wanting and waiting for a sequel for five years. Earlier this year, we finally got the reveal for the sequel, Ghost of Yotei. When this game was revealed, I was so happy and excited that the sequel to Ghost of Tsushima was finally here and that I get to experience it! After playing this game, I can easily say that GoY is a phenomenal game, and it's better than its predecessor in almost every way. Let's talk about the gameplay first. The improvement from GoT's gameplay is MASSIVE. The combat is very different from GoT; instead of having 4 different stances, in Yotei, you get 5 different melee weapons (Wolf Blade, Dual Katana, Yari, Kusarigama, and Odachi). I like the melee weapons way more and prefer them over the stances from GoT. Quickfire and Ranged weapons are improved here as well, especially with the addition of firearms. Although the four main stances from GoT are gone, the Ghost Stance ability remains and returns from GoT (You unlock it by progressing in the story), as well as the addition of the new ability, Onryo's Howl, where you shout and terrify enemies, stunning them. The stealth gameplay in GoY is also different from GoT, and I found the stealth to be more challenging in GoY. The exploration and open world in GoY is SO MUCH BETTER IN EVERY WAY than GoT! The game doesn't hold your hand for you; YOU actually have to explore and see what's out there for you to do. It's so fun to just stop sometimes and see what you can discover with your spyglass. The open world actually feels so alive: random NPC events, a group of horses galloping alongside you in a flowery field, enemy ambushes, it's such an improvement from GoT. You can even camp, start a fire, and cook your own food! The side content in this game is SO MUCH BETTER in GoY. When I first started playing the game, I had BARELY touched the main story content. I've just been mostly doing side stuff for my first few hours in the game. Like in GoT, you have tales and myths, along with a new addition of bounties, where you take down wanted criminals for money and different rewards.  I have to say, there is this one side quest in the game called "The Tale of the Storm Blade" that is absolutely worth doing. That quest is basically a whole tribute to the previous protagonist, Jin Sakai, from GoT. That quest got me so emotional; it was really beautiful. The visuals, details, graphics, and art styles in this game are such a HUGE step-up from GoT. You can just TELL by stopping for a moment and taking in the scenery around you, it's really beautiful. The soundtrack in this game is amazing. Another improvement here, and you can tell, especially in the boss fights, truly incredible. The story is obviously different from GoT, and I think it's better than GoT's story for the most part. It just keeps you engaged and wanting more, and it has some CRAZY twists, and even though I think the ending to GoY was pretty solid, I prefer the ending of GoT. Of course, I can't NOT talk about the protagonist. I think Atsu is great, obviously different from Jin, but she's an amazing character, and she's pretty much on par with Jin as far as protagonists go. (Even though I slightly prefer Jin more than Atsu) They're both great in different ways and for different reasons. To conclude, Ghost of Yotei is a masterpiece, and it's truly a worthy successor of Ghost of Tsushima. This game has exceeded all of my expectations and was worth the long wait. If you loved Ghost of Tsushima like I did, there is no doubt that you will love this game as well. I HIGHLY recommend this game, and I will definitely play this game again, especially when New Game+ drops. One of my personal GOTY contenders. 10/10.

items.quote: As someone who’s played countless action-adventure titles and loved the first Ghost of Tsushima, Ghost of Yotei feels like the natural evolution the series needed. It’s not just bigger—it’s smarter, tighter, and more meaningful in how it delivers its story and world.From the start, it’s clear that Ghost of Yotei isn’t chasing spectacle for spectacle’s sake. Instead, it’s a masterclass in atmosphere and emotional storytelling through gameplay. The flashback system is brilliant—it doesn’t just fill in lore, it connects the player to the protagonist’s past and motivations in real time. You’ll be exploring a ruined shrine one moment and suddenly reliving the event that shaped it the next. It makes every location feel like it carries history, not just pretty **** world design deserves serious praise. Instead of going for a massive open world that spreads itself thin, Yotei focuses on density—every path, clearing, and ridge hides something meaningful. Even when you go off the main road, it feels like the game wants you to, rewarding curiosity with quiet storytelling or beautifully crafted encounters.Narratively, the revenge plot is familiar, but the added political tension between the Matsumae clan, the Ainu, and the mysterious Six of Yotei gives it unexpected depth. You’re not just fighting enemies—you’re navigating a living, conflicted land where every faction has a believable reason to exist. It makes the story feel grounded and mature.Combat is still the heart of the experience, and the swordplay has never felt smoother. Each strike has purpose, and the addition of new weapon types gives combat more layers without losing its sharp focus. The mastery sequences—moments where the game challenges you to perfect timing, precision, and awareness—are the kind of design touches that make you appreciate just how polished this game is.Honestly, it’s hard to find flaws here. Ghost of Yotei doesn’t rely on gimmicks—it relies on craftsmanship, consistency, and emotional weight. It’s the kind of sequel that respects what came before while pushing every system **** Ghost of Tsushima was about honor and identity, Ghost of Yotei is about legacy and consequence. And it’s nothing short of a masterpiece.

Ghost of Yotei Lost the spirit that made Ghost of Tsushima special 

At first glance, Ghost of Yotei looks impressive, but it has lost the soul of the original.
The characters no longer behave like people from historical Japan they act and speak like modern video game protagonists: too direct, too impulsive, too Western in their expression.
What once made Ghost of Tsushima powerful silence, honor, and restraint has been replaced by louder, more mainstream storytelling. The cultural authenticity made the first game unique has given way to a Hollywood-style approach.
You can feel that the game was optimized for a broader audience: less subtlety, more spectacle.
Technically strong and visually beautiful but the soul is gone.

items.quote:
This is my first time posting a review so here goes.
Positives-Ghost Of Yotei in some ways lives up to and even exceeds Tsushima. It is a stunning game with a gorgeous and vibrant colour palette with generally good performance (this is where Yotei surpasses Tsushima). Combat (especially on harder modes) is engaging, fast paced and competitive (this is where Yotei lives up to Tsushima). Some of the side activities are enjoyable, such as learning new songs, painting and bounty hunting. The game really reminds me of a Samurai-Western with vast landscapes that take you through grasslands, wastelands and wartorn frontiers. I recommend playing the game with Japanese VA and with Subtitles for a better experience as Atsu's VA in this version is a lot better, as is many of the other characters you'll meet along the way. Speaking of Atsu, she's a decent enough character (not as compelling or complex as Jin) who's a bit rough around the edges and is quick witted. I think if you look at Ghost Of Yotei as more historically inspired rather than accurate you won't be nitpicking so much.
Negatives-The story and characters really let the game down, as I've just said Atsu is decent enough but everyone else is very forgettable even the villains. The story is very generic and has been done a thousand times before and doesn't compare to Tsushima, Atsu doesn't really have conflict like Jin does at least not something that majorly impacts the story or her Arc. Stealth is VERY undercooked and tacked on, whereas in Tsushima Jin truly felt like a 'Ghost' both in combat and stealth by using gadgets and trickery. Atsu feels more like an undying spirit who goes around carving people up due to the lack of proper stealth mechanics pushing you into combat almost always. Most of your game time is going to be spent exploring the world with the story only taking up a small portion of the game time. Most armours and charms in the game as such are useless unless they promote combat, which is a shame because some look really cool. Progression is middle of the park, I just poured everything into combat, survival and my weapons because the game is again very combat focused rather than anything else. And I found that the map suffers from what a lot of triple A open world games suffers from which is check-boxing, unfortunately I would say that a lot of "side activities" aren't side as the game gets progressively harder and if you don't explore, upgrade and grow your spirit and health bar you will struggle a lot. This became my primary and only incentive to continue exploring rather than because I was actually interested (again that's where the majority of your play time will accumulate). I haven't completed the game and I don't think I will As I'm not interested in doing so, I've currently got 40+ hours in game and I was done about 5-7 hours ago realistically. 
Overall-its a mixed bag with some good highs visually, performance, combat and some side activity wise, but some real lows when it comes to story, charecters, progression and stealth. I wouldn't buy this game at full price, I would advise others to wait till it drops to about 50 or even 40 of whatever currency your country uses and go from there. I'm rating it on the lower end of a 7 so a 7-. 
Thanks for reading, hope this helps

items.quote:
One of the most beautiful games I've ever played. The art direction is simply stunning. In fact it's one of the only games I can say genuinely looks great at 30fps on a base ps5 because of its cinematic nature and smooth optimization. You can play at 60fps if you want, but I prefer the fidelity as the lighting is incredible. You can wander for hours just soaking up the scenery. Lots of attention to detail. Hard to not spend some time in photo mode. 

The revenge story is more nuanced than at first glance, taking a hard look at grief and loss. There are so many quiet moments of reflection that is appreciated.

Meanwhile the world is vast but full of new discoveries, leading to a lot of organic moments.

The gameplay is a lot of fun. Definitely a challenge on lethal mode, but it gets easier and makes progressing your character all the better.

Is it similar to the 1st game, absolutely, and that's a good thing.
items.author: PoetsRobe

items.quote:
Ghost of Yotei is a very good game — not just because it looks beautiful or plays smoothly, but because it tells a story that stays with you. On the surface, it’s a revenge story, but it never really feels like one. Instead, it’s more about family, grief, and the cost of loss. That emotional depth makes it stand out.

The world feels alive in a way few games manage. Everything from sleeping and freezing to eating and surviving adds to the immersion. You don’t just play Ghost of Yotei — you live in it. I especially love how the side quests aren’t just marked on a map like usual; you stumble upon them naturally, which makes exploration feel organic and rewarding. Yes you can turn the markers on, but not to the side quest only to where it leads. The wind is still a brilliant way to guide you.

The characters are another highlight. I felt connected to them, and the ending really hit me. When a game can do that — make you feel something — you know it worked.

I’d call Ghost of Yotei a worthy successor to Ghost of Tsushima. It might not have completely blown me away like fx Red Dead Redemption 2 did, but it left a strong impression nonetheless.

Score: 9/10 — Deeply immersive, emotional, and unforgettable.

items.quote:
This game fails to improve on what made Ghost of Tsushima my favorite game of all time. Here are some of the pros and cons:

Pros:
- Great graphics
- Stable frame rate and performance
- Zeni Hajiki minigame with gambling

Cons:
- Uninteresting story. Much worse than Tsushima.
- Forgettable characters
- Music with little impact compared to Tsushima (Mother’s Song is an exception)
- Huge open areas that feel empty (like typical Ubisoft games).
- Only a few new activities and once you’ve played every of the 12 activities a few times it’s very boring. Quests are the same. Very Ubisoft.
- revamped combat. They replaced stances with new weapons that basically has the exact same function; to adapt to enemies. Stances made sense, whereas this just feels strange.
- more difficult to make armor builds with charms etc as all of it is situational.
- armors don’t look nearly as good as in Tsushima
- MC doesn’t look inspiring, and also has a dull personality with little progression.

Overall this game lacks much of the soul that made Tsushima so great. This is not a review to hurt woke or whatever btw. I was genuinely interested in this game, and now I’m genuinely disappointed with the game. It’s not bad, but it’s not great. It feels too much like Ubisoft, albeit a slightly more refined and less buggy version of Ubisoft. This is very unfortunate as I’ve been looking forward to the sequel for years. I’m not even sure if I’ll end up completing platinum as i usually do with these type of games.

So in short, I’m disappointed.
Good, but not great.
5/10

An honest and neutral review with minor spoilers.

The good. 
Excellent combat, weapons variations to fit your style of play. Better map system. Good story with some great moments. 

The bad
Weird story and dialog elements. Some “discoveries” should have come early. Some questions like “where is the mother” to a young girl or her father - typically would get asked earlier. Feels like RDR2 in Japan but with less than half the charm. (Even the resting against the horse is a direct lift). 

The ugly. 
Unlike RDR2, stranger interaction and discoveries are mundane. Dialogs are uninteresting by comparison. AI is weak at times, graphics (always compromised due to open world) feel 2020-ish. 

Conclusion. 
I would give it a 7.5 but not 8. If you’re a fan of games like the Witcher 3 or RDR 2 you will really like this but there’s nothing original going on here.

items.quote:
Après une cinquantaine d’heures passées sur Ghost of Yōtei, je peux dire que c’est une aventure incroyable, aussi belle **** n’est pas une révolution totale, mais une évolution maîtrisée et profonde de Ghost of Tsushima. **** Punch nous transporte cette fois dans un Japon plus froid, plus spirituel, dominé par la neige et la vengeance, avec une ambiance visuelle tout simplement **** jeu impressionne dès les premières minutes : les paysages enneigés du mont Yōtei sont magnifiques, la lumière, la météo et les effets de vent donnent une vraie vie au monde. L’exploration est un pur plaisir, chaque détour cache un secret, une ruine, un combat ou un moment contemplatif. Même après 50h, j’ai encore énormément de choses à faire, ce qui est **** système de combat est un gros point fort. Ici, pas de postures à changer comme dans Tsushima : chaque arme possède désormais sa posture **** kusarigama (fouet-lame) est parfait contre les ennemis équipés de boucliers, l’odachi (grande épée) excelle contre les brutes, et chaque arme impose son propre style.C’est un choix brillant : le gameplay devient plus fluide, plus instinctif et encore plus tactique. Chaque duel se joue sur la précision, le timing et la lecture des mouvements adverses. Quand tout s’enchaîne parfaitement, la sensation de puissance est grisante.Atsu, la protagoniste, est une héroïne marquante. Forte, blessée, et humaine, elle porte une histoire de vengeance bien écrite et chargée d’émotion. Les dialogues et les cinématiques sont d’un excellent niveau, portés par une bande-son japonaise splendide et une mise en scène soignée.Techniquement, le jeu est superbe. Quelques **** bugs ou soucis de caméra subsistent, mais rien qui gâche l’expérience. Le rythme du scénario connaît quelques baisses, et certaines activités secondaires se répètent un peu, mais globalement l’équilibre est bon.Ghost of Yōtei n’est pas qu’un jeu d’action, c’est une expérience sensorielle et spirituelle, un voyage dans un Japon rude et poétique. C’est un monde dans lequel on se perd facilement, tant la beauté, le son et l’atmosphère **** attendant le mode multijoueur (qui promet d’ajouter encore beaucoup de contenu), le solo à lui seul justifie pleinement l’aventure. Note finale : 8.5 / 10 Un jeu magnifique, profond et inspiré. Il ne change pas tout, mais il perfectionne presque **** œuvre à ne pas manquer pour les fans de Tsushima et de belles aventures japonaises.

(Avis personnel – MrKrakotte sur YouTube)

items.quote: So I finished Ghost of Yotei. Controversies aside, judging it fairly, I would rate my experience a 6/10. To be blunt I’ve plaid this exact game before. It was called Ghost of Tushima. Ghost of Tushima had a much better plot and the small combat improvements in Ghost of Yotei, don’t make me feel that that this is a must play for fans of the original. The good: The music and graphics are in Yotei are stunning, as is to be expected when there’s a leap in console generation. I like how the dualsense has different vibration styles depending on what happens in the game. There are minor combat changes like disarming that are small improvements on the original game. The bad: You can tell that this is a game that started as DLC for the original and should have stayed as DLC. The story is very basic and the characters lack personality. Six samurai kill your family and now you need to and kill them. This plot is ripped from several pre-existing Japanese samurai films and of course Kill Bill (thinking about it, it parodies the plot of Kill Bill a lot). It never surprised me with what happened in the plot and never gets interesting. So a total opposite to Ghost of Tushima which may not have had the best directed cutscenes but the plot was at least interesting and unique. I also don't particularly like how only one of the six samurais deserved forgiveness, of course it’s the only female samurai in the group and of course she ends up being the love interest. Why have all Sony games in the past decade that stared women ended up with gay leads and always follow the "revenge is bad" plot? These have been done to death. It's a massive let down when personally all I really wanted was a direct sequel to the original GOT. The gameplay improvements are minor. If like me you played Ghost of Tushima for 60+ hours and got the platinum, then there isn’t enough here to make you want to commit to another 60+ hours to 100% complete it. It’s pretty much the same open world and the same combat. Sure disarms and separated skill trees add some improvements but there’s equally a large number of stupid or silly changes. The roar technique looks ridiculous. Atsu yells and all the male samurai either fall over of just stand there over reacting. It totally breaks the immersion. In fact most of the way the fight cerography works looks silly. Atsu shouldn’t be able to match strength with men who have visibly thicker more muscular arms than her, but there are times when she’s matching or out powering them in strength. It looks silly. Instead the animations should have been based on her being faster that them, tricking or outsmarting them, or using another advantage like a second weapon. It looks as silly as when Chloe Fraser had Nathan Drakes exact move set in Uncharted The Lost Legacy. A lot of open world improvements are also “filler” content. You can stroke the wolf or fish or cut grass with your sword. But seriously this just wastes time. It doesn’t give players a better experience, it just fills in the run time. TLDR is that this game isn’t as good as the original Ghost of Tushima and is likely to disappoint fans. I really do feel like **** needs to take a look at whoever wrote the plot for this game and question why they allowed them to go with this narrative, why they moved away from Jin or at least didn’t set the game directly after the events of his. Game companies also need to realise that open world fatigue is real and that you can’t just recycle the last open world game with minimal improvements. It’s crazy many games fail these days due to bad plots.

items.quote: The hack and slash is still decent fun, the story is serviceable if uninspired, and there are big beautiful landscapes to explore.  But the open-world structure of this game is very formulaic and the formula is very dated in 2025.  The combat is not really deep enough to remain engaging across the huge scale of the game; there are new primary and secondary weapons, but there are only so many ways you can eviscerate endless copies of the same enemies.  Combined with the repetitive nature of open-world box checking, this leads to a game which can struggle to stay interesting.  The narrative is more or less fine but it feels like it was written by a huge team.  Individual quests and cutscenes are well written, but somehow they don't cohere very well and the whole is less than the sum of its parts.  Nothing in this game is offensively bad.  The main quests in particular have some really well-done action sequences.  There were times when I found it hard to stop playing.  But it's all a bit paint-by-numbers, a good-enough iteration on games we've played before, which shows little ambition to be more than that.

items.quote:
Ghost of Yōtei is nothing short of breathtaking — a rare gem that transcends the boundary between video game and interactive art. From the moment you step foot on the snowey slopes of Mount Yōtei, it’s clear this isn’t just another open-world samurai tale — it’s a soulful journey about resilience, honor, and the quiet poetry of nature.

Visually, the game is a triumph. Every sunrise over frozen ridges and every gust of mountain wind feels alive, painted with an artist’s precision and a poet’s heart. The new lighting engine and weather effects make Hokkaido feel untamed and spiritual — it’s the kind of environment that begs you to stop, breathe, and simply exist within it.

Combat is deeply satisfying — an evolution of Ghost of Tsushima’s elegance with even sharper precision and flow. Every parry, strike, and stealth encounter carries weight and emotion. The addition of environmental combat (sliding on ice, ambushing from snowdrifts) makes battles feel cinematic yet personal. The “Reliquaries” and “Lighthouse Trials” expand the game’s meditative puzzle-solving side, rewarding patience and mindfulness as much as skill.

The story — without spoilers — is profoundly human. It’s a narrative of loss, courage, and finding peace in the face of despair. The writing is mature and restrained, supported by world-class performances and a score that blends traditional Japanese instrumentation with haunting ambient melodies.

What truly sets Ghost of Yōtei apart is its balance between serenity and intensity. One moment you’re dueling beneath drifting cherry blossoms; the next, you’re meditating beside a frozen lake as foxes watch from afar. It’s the kind of game that stays with you long after the credits roll — not because of bombastic twists, but because it makes you feel something rare: peace.

Ghost of Yōtei is a generation-defining achievement — a symphony of art direction, emotional storytelling, and masterful design. It’s not only one of the best PlayStation exclusives ever made — it’s one of the most beautiful games of all time.

After several hours (and many more to come), Ghost of Yōtei proves itself a worthy successor to Ghost of Tsushima — one that refines rather than reinvents, but does so with style, emotional weight, and impressive polish.

Ghost of Yōtei doesn’t aim to revolutionize open-world action gaming — but it doesn’t need to. What it does do is take the strong foundation laid by Tsushima, iterate in meaningful ways, and tell a more introspective, character-driven story. It’s stylish, immersive, and often moving. If you were hesitant about jumping back into this world, Yōtei gives you a compelling reason to return.

items.quote:
I usually compare games to their predecessors so Im basing my review on GOT.
Gameplay - 5/10. It would have been better to learn different techniques for the katana, or a different weapon compared to magical weapons sprouting from nowhere
Story 2/10 - Very lazy revenge arc, a lot of plot holes especially in the villains actions. 
Graphics 6/10 - slight improvement from GOT, but really need to look for it
World 7/10 - Better than GOT in some regards. Not in most tho 

Basically its a lazy sequel to GOT, without the moral compass of a samurai. 
Gameplay is basically the same, with minimal changes due to the switch between stances and different weapons. The targeting system in melee is very janky. Also the switch between weapons compared to stances looks very unrealistic. The weapons are ok, but they all feel the same. Button mash, with good timing gets you the result you want. So its pointless IMO. Only thing that is new and I like a lot are the bounties even tho they get repetitive after a while.
Graphics just like the gameplay, are very similar to GoT with minimal improvements here and there. Foliage reacts the same, water is as bad as it was in GOT. Animations are mostly kept the same as GOT which is very disappointing. 
World Design is slightly better, with the "town" hubs feeling more lived in. Only issue is that they are much smaller than the ones in GoT so I kept thinking where do most of the NPC's sleep. 
Story is way worse. There is an opportunity to go with a different character -Jibei. He has the more compelling story out of the twins, and would fit the parameters we expected from a sequel of GOT. Atsu on the other hand is bearable, compared to the online uproar. There are moments where you can see that her decisions are terrible and costing countless people lives, but somehow magically it all works out to make her to be the hero. But the main problem if we are comparing Jin and Atsu is that Jin had a moral compass and was likeable. Atsu is not likeable. Only reason that NPC's seem to react positively to her in the game is that she is a killer. Jin on the other hand had more pure motivations in his actions. There is not a lot of the LGBT crap so far, but Im barely 30% in my progress so I hope that does not change.
Bottom Line
Unnecessary move to a character that no one will like, and a basic revenge story arc that we have seen a million times. Stale gameplay and stale graphics do not help the game out. 
I usually review games when I'm done. But this one I had to jump in early with my main concern pre-purchase being is it worth it. Answer is that so far I regret purchasing the game full price and not waiting for the discounted offers that will surely show up in the next few months.

Although you can unlock most of the weapons early, it's clearly intended that you get them in a certain order (because of the enemy types you encounter while unlocking them or in the region they are).

Fighting is good but playing in hard or lethal difficulty feels off (perfect parry windows seems not consistent while perfect dodging feels consistent). The swapping weapons is more interesting than the stances from Tsushima and fights feel more dangerous (even in the end of the game with all perks unlocks).

Some mechanics from Tsushima are unfortunately missing (fully exploring the zone map when fully liberated, challenges while capturing camps for example).

items.quote:
While Ghost of Tsushima was really, REALLY good, this game was just really good. The only reason why it's not really any higher than an 8 for me, is that the story isn't anything special and at times (mainly at the end) very, VERY predictable. And, to be honest, I think the game at times doesn't really look that different. There are a decent amount of reused animations in this game, which personally bothers me.

Now, "woke" is definitely something that is going to pop up from time-to-time with the conversation surrounding this game, and I have to say...those people are wrong. Atsu is never an annoying, "Nathan Drake" Mary Sue that a lot of female characters tend to be nowadays. She's definitely like Jin in the sense that she kind of is "boring", but she does have some endearing, sweet, and funny moments along with some actually cool one-liners after beating enemies. There's only really 2 things that I can think of that could be "woke"...number 1: Atsu being a woman is brought up **** it's 1627. In feudal Japan. So it's honestly very realistic and done correctly in a way that doesn't make you roll your eyes and sigh. And number 2: There is KIND OF, MAYBE, POSSIBLY a homosexual relationship in the game. But it's honestly so up in the air, that I have trouble even saying that with 100% certainty. And even if that were the **** relationship is done very, VERY well. In fact, I at times found it a LITTLE more believable than Jin/Yuna. Just a little.

With that being said...music, acting, art direction, gameplay, side quests, some of the story, and open world are all either just as good or HUGE step ups from the last game. There is very much NOT a shortage of really cool moments, aka, "sauce" in this game as well. I found myself having to pause and just laugh at how absolutely awesome, or cinematic certain things were. I genuinely was caught off guard by some of the story beats, and the side quests are really emotionally driven and well written. The navigation is also much, MUCH better, as birds and the guiding wind won't lead you off cliffs or up mountains anymore, and will now guide you to climbable areas or paths. The combat MAY be hit or miss depending on how you view the new "swap weapons" system, but I loved it. It's all still fluid as ever and feels satisfying when you get REALLY good at it. The Japanese dub being synced with the game is also very, VERY nice and is a sign of great respect from the developers toward the country the game is based in. They absolutely did not have to do that but did. In terms of performance, I've nearly 100% the game, and recently started a second playthrough...never crashed ONCE or had any real drops in frames that I could notice. 

Ghost of Yotei really is just the last one but better in almost every. Single. Way. Almost. If you're not turned off by the main lead's politics, a crappy dev, and familiarity, I'd definitely recommend this game.

items.quote:
Combat is generally fun, though I'm not a gigantic fan of weapon swapping as a core mechanic.

Exploration is decent, though not to the extent of the reigning king, Skyrim. Which is obviously a personal opinion.

Dialog and voice acting is good, even great (English).

Storyline is blah.  Another revenge plot line, similar plot points to GoT, such as the early game Deus Ex loss to the final boss early.  Which felt particularly noticeable.   I honestly hate forced losses, scripted forced failure.

Music is acceptable, though nothing stuck in my head like with Clair Obscur.   

Here is where I'll get flak. There is a problem with modern female protagonist games.   I don't think the messaging is compatible with the vehicle, particularly a historical fiction.

There is some active feminist messaging here, but it's soft in the wrong ways. We see some patronizing from male characters, and we get some gratifying push back from the female MC, but it really avoids the harsher historical reality.  They have the massacres, the abuse of the "peasantry" but avoid what would actually be happening to the women when bandits sack a village. They avoid what would actually be the threat a lone female MC would have to deal with.  I'm not sure I can even say it here, as it's something that has to be airbrushed over even in public commentary.

Like so many female protagonist action games, the MC feels like a male protagonist.  Male levels of physical strength, tomboy characterization, subtle, or even blatant, misandry...  the environment can be unrealistically beautiful but the characters must be grounded in reality appearance wise.

The moment her twin brother was revealed to be alive I could predict his entire arc, including his death, it was excruciatingly predictable and another Deus Ex.

I ask myself who the target audience exactly is.   If it is intended for young women who like action combat games and are invested in modern feminist ideology, then it's spot on.  Yet how large is that audience?

If it's intended for a general audience, then I think in the end it will not succeed as well.   The primary consumers of mature rated action combat games remains predominantly young male adults.  This is just a reality, not a political thing.

In the end, like other female MC combat games, you can't really have a HEA ending.   The traditional "happily ever after" ending simply not compatible with the ideological messaging.   No meeting a mate, perhaps non-combatant like her father, and raising some kids.  No retired aunt in her brothers household teaching her nieces and nephews the sword....

Nope.  Any and all potential male contemporaries need to be dead or irrelevant at the end.  

This is another piece of media that is more interested in messaging than financial success.

Some advice for these studios.  Go whole hog with the ideology.  Create a fantasy world dominated by women, complete role reversal, men are weaker, woman run the show, men raise the children and take on the "feminine" gender roles.  Pivot the game loop more towards dialog, exploration, and relationships, and less towards combat.

This will appeal to your apparent target audience more directly and will probably actually do really well in the market in comparison.

Stop expecting young men to get excited about a game that tells them they sorta ****.

items.quote:
Combat & Visuals: Ghost of Yōtei shines with its fluid and satisfying combat mechanics. Every encounter feels intense and rewarding. The graphics are absolutely gorgeous — from the character models to the breathtaking landscapes, it's one of the most visually impressive games out there. 

Open World & Missions: The open world is well-crafted and immersive, offering plenty to explore. Main missions are solid, and side quests add flavor, though some of them start to feel repetitive after a while. That repetition slightly affects the pacing, especially for completionists. 

Storyline: The story is enjoyable and emotionally engaging, but a bit predictable. It doesn’t quite match the depth or impact of the original game’s narrative, and it feels like the developers didn’t push the story as far as they could have. 

Final Verdict: Ghost of Yōtei is a very fun and polished experience. However, it might have worked better as a DLC rather than a full standalone release. Still, it’s a must-play for fans of samurai action and open-world adventures.

items.quote: At first I wasn't sure if I was going to buy it, as much as I enjoyed Ghost Of Tushima by the end it did just feel like 'Samurai Far-Cry' which isn't bad but it was repetitive. If I was to give GOT a score it would be a solid 7.5/10. But decided to give Yotei a shot, at the very least had have some fun. However, Yotei has completely blown me away, if I had to describe it 'Red Dead Redemption meets Ghost of Tushima' is the perfect description. The open world is easily one of the best in gaming up there with Breath Of The Wild, Elden Ring and Red Dead Redemption 2. The amount of unique content that you find is truly breathtaking, after the intro I spent over 25 hours getting side tracked from the main story, and its not like Assassin'sCreed where it feels bloated, its natural and exciting. Id love to go into more details but this world is better explored yourself. Honestly its a night and day difference to Tushima. Then you have Atsu who is easily one of the better written female protagonists we have had in years. Shes not cocky or overly sure of herself but at the same time confident. The story is also a lot more personal this time around I don't want to go into spoilers but it's fantastic! Combat is also improved with multiple new weapons, the ability to shoot guns and throw enemies dropped weapons, but you can also be disarmed yourself and have to avoid attacks until you retrieve your weapon (if you have multiple weapons you can always switch to that if needed)... Controversy: Since the announcement of GOY there were people trying to downplay the quality of the game due to the lead character being a women, This was made worse when they discovered the lead actress was Erika Ishii, an actress with over 100 videogame credits, but because of her eccentric and openly gay personality they decided to create a smear campaign against her and the game (anything for views and likes huh?) it did slow down but then the assassination of Charlie Kirk happened and thousands of people either celebrated or made jokes. One of those people unfortunately was an Artist at **** Punch, fortunately she was promptly fired within 48 hours of the disgusting and quite frankly Selfish comment, they would of been aware of the smear campaign against the game, to add fuel to the fire and bring a whole tonne of hate towards your colleagues is just really shortsighted. However I judge art on the art not by who made it. Overall GOY is a thrilling revenge tale set in one of the best open worlds ever made, it sits firmly amongst the pantheon of other amazing open world games and is an absolute must play.

items.quote: Ghost of Yotei is a mind-blowing sequel to Ghost of Tsushima, set 300 years later with a new protagonist, Atsu. Its narrative centers on a revenge-driven non-linear kill list, allowing players to hunt targets in any order. The combat abandons traditional stances for a brutal, multi-weapon arsenal, with katana, nodachi, kusarigama, and more. Battles feel raw and vicious, blending stealth and open combat seamlessly. The world of Yotei is bleak yet breathtaking, filled with handcrafted quests, mythic tales, and atmospheric landscapes. While some side quest repetition and UI hand-holding remain, the overall design evolves the Tsushima formula with meaningful player choice and visceral gameplay. Ghost of Yotei is not just more of the same, but a bold and beautiful evolution of the series.

items.quote:
Walking and fish cooking simulator with cut scenes. I have no idea what this was supposed to be, but a game worth $5 it ain't.

Far from it. Putting aside the hype train and the glossy trailers, what you get is a shiny veneer trying desperately to gloss over a lot of rough edges. And trust me, I see those edges — like a patch of uncut grass in a manicured lawn, glaring and ugly. At least we can cut grass...

The narrative leans too hard on clichés: grief, vengeance, betrayal, tortured relationships. There’s very little here that surprises, and characters feel more like cardboard cutouts than real people.

Early chapters drag, middle arcs lurch between melodrama and filler, and the finale feels rushed. It’s like they ran out of grass to mow ahead of deadline — some parts are neat and trimmed, others wild, overgrown, left to be resolved offscreen.

The vistas are postcards; the gameplay in those spaces is empty. Roaming for half an hour to find something meaningful becomes tedious.

items.quote:
The combat is phenomenal, and the shift from stances to multiple weapons adds considerable novelty.  The combat feels great, fluid and solid.  

The overall arc of the story is, of course, somewhat predictable (it is a revenge story after all; there are only so many ways it can go), but it's still well-executed with some nice twists.

The graphics are, on the whole, stunning. One reviewer mentioned that this is a game that you can pause at almost any moment and the result would be fit for a wallpaper. I agree with this assessment. The scenery is gorgeous, and the lighting and environmental effects are top-notch, as is the motion and character animation. My only nits with the graphics are that some random NPCs look a bit flat (i.e. skin shading), and during very fast camera cuts, you can sometimes see a couple of frames of asset loading.  On the other hand, the performance is very solid, and the game, on the whole, simply looks phenomenal.  The range and diversity of different "biomes" is also truly impressive, and gives the game a much more expansive feel and varied look than Tsushima. Yet, that diversity of environments doesn't come at the cost of visual awe or artistic flair; they all look splendid.

This is a great game that shares a spiritual lineage with Tsushima, but that improves on that game in almost every way. The story is well, executed, the world is open and alive, but still driven by the story, the graphics are gorgeous, and the combat feels amazing.  There are a few small nits one can make, or imperfections one can find when applying scrutiny, but they are relatively minor and rare. SP has a masterpiece in Ghost of Yotei, and it's well worth the price of admission.
